_comment: Claude Code MCP configuration — Graphiti HTTPS front door and Context7 docs.
Authority: environment/agents/adapters/claude-code/mcp.template.json is the
SINGLE canonical owner. The project-scope .mcp.json is RENDERED from this file
by ops/scripts/claude_projection.py (domain: mcp) and drift-checked — it is a
projection, never a second authority.
NO CREDENTIAL VALUES in this file, in .mcp.json, or in the account variables
field. Transport credentials are referenced as ${VAR} only, exactly like
${GRAPHITI_MCP_URL}: the platform proxies a value into the variable when it
has one to proxy, Claude Code expands it at load, and nothing is ever written
down. web/setup.bootstrap.sh therefore does not sweep GRAPHITI_MCP_TOKEN or
CONTEXT7_API_KEY — the same reasoning that keeps GH_TOKEN unswept there.
_requires_env on a server: the server renders only when every listed variable
is set and non-empty. _optional_headers: {VAR: {header: value}} merges those
headers only when VAR is set and non-empty. Both are private keys, stripped
from the render like _comment. They exist so an unproxied session degrades to
the previous behaviour instead of emitting a server that cannot authenticate:
Graphiti stays unauthenticated (which is how the front door works today) and
Context7 is simply absent, with the obligation on skill l9-context7-docs per
rules/22-context7-auto-invoke.
STILL FORBIDDEN: a literal token value anywhere in this file or in the account
variables field, the retired HTTP l9-shared-memory side door, L9_MEMORY_HTTP_*
lifecycle env, and ${L9_CAPABILITY_BROKER_URL}/mcp/graphiti (never shipped).
